description.content: Pre-measure all columns and rows in a Grid. Typically cells are only measured as needed and estimated sizes are used for cells that have not yet been measured. This method ensures that the next call to getTotalSize() returns an exact size (as opposed to just an estimated one).

description.content: Recomputes row heights and column widths after the specified index (both default to 0). This function should be called if dynamic column or row sizes have changed but nothing else has. Since Grid only receives columnCount and rowCount it has no way of detecting when the underlying data changes. This method will also force a render cycle to ensure that the updated measurements are reflected in the rendered grid.

methods.html: recomputeGridSize(params?: { columnIndex?: number; rowIndex?: number }): void;
methods.name: recomputeGridSize

description.content: Ensure the specified column and/or row is visible (scrolling if necessary). This method can be used to safely scroll back to a cell that a user has scrolled away from even if it was previously scrolled to. The align parameter (default "auto") controls the alignment of the cell: "auto" scrolls the least amount possible to ensure that the specified cell is fully visible (a cell larger than the Grid is aligned to its start, so that its start is visible); "start" aligns the cell to the top/left of the Grid and "end" to the bottom/right; "center" aligns the cell in the middle of the Grid. This is a one-time scroll: the cell is not kept in view afterwards (e.g. if the Grid's size or its cell sizes change). Cells that haven't been measured yet (e.g. by CellMeasurer) are positioned using their estimated sizes. Nothing is scrolled while the Grid's width or height is 0. The column is ignored for single-column grids (e.g. List, Table). If the Grid has a scrollElement, the scroll element (e.g. the window) is scrolled vertically instead.

description.content: Scroll to the specified offset(s); an omitted offset is left unchanged. Offsets are clamped to the scrollable range. Calling this method with the current offsets does nothing. If the Grid has a scrollElement, scrollTop scrolls the scroll element (e.g. the window) instead (to the position at which the Grid is scrolled by scrollTop).
